# Global ordinary depth stability by an inscribed-simplex normalization

For every d>=2 there is a finite A_d>0 such that every full-dimensional
compact convex body K in R^d and every minimum-volume enclosing simplex
S satisfy

    1-|K|/|S| <=A_d[D(K)-Gamma_d],
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.                           (1)

Here D(K) is normalized maximum ordinary halfspace depth. Consequently
the same upper bound controls cap distance and total variation between
the uniform laws of K and S. This is an ordinary continuous stability
theorem, not a mixed-integer conclusion. Its two geometric inputs are
the proved local theorem in
`candidate c62d1cc13c75171f` and the classical
Grunbaum equality consequence D(K)=Gamma_d iff K is a simplex, proved
in `candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`.

The argument below supplies the compactness and uniformity needed to
turn the local estimate into a global one. It does not use John's
theorem or presume compactness of unnormalized bodies.

## 1. An attained inscribed simplex gives a compact normalization

Write T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), V=|T|=1/d!, with barycentric functions
lambda_0,...,lambda_d. The volume of conv(x_0,...,x_d) is continuous
on the compact set K^(d+1); it has a positive maximum because K has
interior. Choose an attaining tuple and send its simplex to T by an
invertible affine map. After this ordinary normalization,

    T subset K,
    every simplex with vertices in K has volume at most V.  (2)

For any x in K, replace the i-th vertex of T by x. The resulting
simplex has volume |lambda_i(x)|V, by the affine determinant formula.
It is inscribed in K, so (2) implies |lambda_i(x)|<=1. Therefore

    K subset P={x:|lambda_i(x)|<=1 for every i}.    (3)

The set P is compact: its last d inequalities put each coordinate in
[-1,1], and it is closed. Thus all normalized bodies belong to

    A={convex compact K:T subset K subset P,
                 all simplices inscribed in K have volume<=V}. (4)

This class is compact in Hausdorff distance. Indeed compact convex
subsets of the fixed compact box have Hausdorff-convergent subsequences
(the usual elementary Blaschke selection theorem). Both inclusions are
preserved. If K_l converge to K and x_0,...,x_d belong to K, choose
x_(i,l) in K_l converging to x_i. Determinant continuity preserves the
last inequality in (4), so the class is closed. Every member contains
T and hence is full dimensional with volume at least V.

The ONLY simplex in A is T. If K itself is a simplex, its volume is
at most V by the inscribed-simplex condition and at least V by T subset
K. An enclosing full-dimensional convex body of equal volume must
coincide with T: any point outside T creates a cone of positive volume
beyond at least one of its facets. Hence K=T.

## 2. A positive depth gap off a fixed neighborhood

On A, normalized uniform volume measures vary continuously in total
variation under Hausdorff convergence. To see this, the indicator
functions converge off the limiting convex body's boundary: an exterior
point is eventually exterior, while an interior point is eventually
interior, for example by supporting inequalities and a small interior
ball around it. The boundary has Lebesgue measure zero, all indicators
are bounded by the fixed box indicator, and volumes are bounded below
by V. Dominated convergence therefore gives the asserted normalized
total variation convergence.

For any two probability measures, their halfspace-depth functions at
EVERY ambient point differ by at most their total variation distance.
Taking suprema over all ambient points gives the same bound for maximum
depth. For full-dimensional uniform convex bodies the supremum is an
attained interior maximum, by continuity of cap volumes and positivity
at the centroid. Thus D(K) is continuous on A.

Let epsilon_d>0 be the fixed local radius from the local theorem, and
consider the compact subset

    A_far={K in A:dist_H,infinity(K,T)>=epsilon_d}.

If it is nonempty, continuity gives an attained minimum

    eta_d=min_(K in A_far)[D(K)-Gamma_d].           (5)

Classical Grunbaum makes this nonnegative. Equality would force K to
be a simplex; Section1 then forces K=T, contrary to membership in
A_far. Consequently eta_d>0. If A_far is empty, simply set eta_d=1;
no far-body estimate will be needed. This convention avoids an infimum
over the empty set.

## 3. The global estimate and its limitations

Set

    c_d=[1-d^(1-d)]/[(d-1)^2(d+1)],
    A_d=max{4/(Gamma_d*c_d),1/eta_d}.              (6)

Take any normalized K in A, and an arbitrary minimum-volume enclosing
simplex S, whose existence is proved in
`candidate 783495094e97ee67`.
If dist_H,infinity(K,T)<=epsilon_d, the local theorem applies to EVERY
such minimizer, giving (1) with the first constant in (6). Otherwise
K belongs to A_far, and

    1-|K|/|S|<=1<=[D(K)-Gamma_d]/eta_d,

which gives (1) with the other constant. The possible overlap at the
distance boundary causes no issue. Applying the inverse affine map
from Section1 preserves all volume ratios, halfspace depths, and
minimum-volume enclosing simplices, so (1) holds for the original K.

For nested uniform bodies the total variation distance is exactly
1-|K|/|S|, and cap distance is at most this amount. This proves the
claimed comparisons. If D(K)=Gamma_d, the estimate also recovers K=S.
For d=1 every convex body is an interval and S=K, so the assertion is
trivial with any positive A_1; no expression in (6) is used there.

The constant A_d is proved finite and depends only on d. Its second
term is an attained geometric minimum, not an explicit closed formula.
The local coefficient and radius are supplied separately. No uniformity
in d and no mixed-integer center or fiber compatibility is asserted.

# Global ordinary depth stability by an inscribed-simplex normalization

**Ordinary maximum-depth stability via enclosing-simplex volume**

For each fixed d>=2 there is a finite dimension-only constant C_d such that, for a d-dimensional convex body K and every minimum-volume enclosing simplex T, 1-|K|/|T| <= C_d (D(K)-Gamma_d), where D(K) is ordinary maximum normalized halfspace depth.

Scope limits: Ordinary continuous bodies only. Depends on the separately proved local quantitative theorem, enclosing-simplex existence, and equality rigidity cited in the source. The compactness constant is not explicit; this audit does not re-prove those dependencies.
